The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book's model answer stops at 'specialised structures called gemmae'; the card adds the standard gemma-cup detail (NCERT) that a 2-mark answer needs.

insider_note: Most answers stop at the word gemmae; the second mark needs the detail — green multicellular buds formed in gemma cups on the thallus.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The means: gemmae
lines: fragmentation of the thallus, and by
steps.why: The one word the question is testing is gemmae; fragmentation is the second standard route for liverworts.
common_mistakes: Writing 'spores' — spore formation is asexual reproduction, not vegetative.
Misspelling gemmae (it has two m's and ends in -ae).
steps.memory_tip: Two routes: the body breaks (fragmentation) or the body buds (gemmae).
steps.margin_note: Fragmentation + gemmae — one sentence carries the mark.

steps.label: What gemmae are
lines: They form in small cups (gemma cups) on
the thallus. A gemma separates from the
parent and germinates into a new
steps.why: The mark is for what a gemma is and what it does: a bud that separates and germinates — no gametes at any point, which is why this is vegetative reproduction.
common_mistakes: Calling gemmae unicellular — they are multicellular buds.
Saying gemmae are formed by fertilization — no gametes are involved.
steps.memory_tip: Three g-words in order: gemma, gemma cup, germinate.
steps.margin_note: Definition line + where they form + what they do.
